script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: forgiveness

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. TECHNOLOGY COMPANY - DAY

Brightly lit open-plan office hums with activity. CUBICLES filled with employees typing away at their computers.

Suddenly, STEVE (30s, an employee) storms into the office, red-faced. He marches up to JENNY (30s, a colleague), who is sitting at her desk, calmly typing.

STEVE
(angrily)
How could you do that to me, Jenny? I trusted you!

Jenny looks up, surprised, but doesn't rise from her seat.

JENNY
(quietly)
Steve, I didn't mean to hurt you. I thought you'd understand.

Steve's face twists in anger. He reaches into his pocket and pulls out a sheet of paper.

STEVE
(angrily)
This was our project. Our chance to make a difference. And you went behind my back and gave it to Mark?

Jenny flinches, looking down at her hands.

JENNY
(softly)
Steve, I know it looks bad, but Mark is a valuable asset to the team. He brought new ideas, and together, we could have made something amazing.

Steve takes a deep breath, his anger beginning to dissipate.

STEVE
(sighing)
I guess you're right. But I can't just forget about this. I need some time to process it.

Jenny nods sympathetically.

JENNY
Of course, Steve. Take all the time you need.

Steve turns on his heel and storms out of the office, leaving Jenny sitting at her desk, looking worried.

INT. COFFEE SHOP - LATER

Steve sits alone at a table, staring into the depths of his coffee cup. Across the room, he sees Jenny enter, carrying a takeout box. She scans the room, and when she spots Steve, she hesitates, then makes her way over to him.

JENNY
(approaching)
Steve, I've been thinking about what happened. And I want to apologize. I never meant to betray your trust. It was a mistake.

Steve looks up at her, his face still etched with anger and hurt.

STEVE
(angrily)
You think a simple apology can make things right? I trusted you, Jenny. You were my partner, my friend. And you stabbed me in the back.

Jenny takes a deep breath, trying to keep her voice steady.

JENNY
I know I hurt you, Steve. And I'm truly sorry. But if we both keep holding onto this anger, we'll never move forward. We'll never be able to work together again. And that would be a shame, because we've accomplished great things as a team.

Steve looks at her, unsure.

STEVE
I don't know, Jenny. I just don't know.

Jenny reaches out and takes Steve's hand.

JENNY
(softly)
Please, Steve. Give me a chance to make things right. To prove that I'm worthy of your trust again.

Steve hesitates, then nods.

STEVE
(sighing)
Alright, Jenny. I'll give you a chance.

Jenny smiles, relieved.

JENNY
Thank you, Steve. I won't let you down again.

INT. TECHNOLOGY COMPANY - DAY

The office is once again buzzing with activity. Steve and Jenny sit side by side at their desks, working together on a new project. They exchange smiles and small talk, and it's clear that they've moved past their disagreement.

As they work, the camera pulls back, revealing the rest of the team in their cubicles, typing away at their computers. The office is once again a hive of productivity and collaboration.

FADE OUT.

THE END.
